Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

ggcircos 0.1.0

First release of the rewrite. The package is now built on layout as data: circos_layout() computes every node arc and every link’s angular slot once, and the geoms read that table instead of managing their own canvas. Requires ggplot2 >= 4.0 (it is built on coord_radial()).

Core

  • ggcircos() builds the layout and returns a plain ggplot object; add layers to it. Accepts a correlation matrix, a link table, or an igraph / tbl_graph.
  • geom_chord() — ribbons or curves between node slots; fill/colour work with any ggplot2 scale and legend.
  • geom_node_arc(), geom_node_text(), geom_node_point() — the node ring.
  • geom_track() — columns, bars, areas, boxplots, violins, density curves, points, tiles or text in a radial band; geom_track_axis() — a readable ruler on a band. geom = "violin" fills each node’s density outline with the value along the radius; geom = "density" draws the same density as an open ridgeline curve, so several distributions can share one band. Both take n, adjust and trim, passed to stats::density().
  • sectors = groups nodes into sectors with a wider gap; geom_sector_label() labels them.
  • weight = makes the geometry follow the values, the way circlize::chordDiagram() does: node arcs proportional to the weight they carry and slots proportional to their link’s weight (weight = r on a matrix). Left unset, every node keeps an equal arc and every link an equal share, as before.
  • layout_nodes(), layout_links(), layout_sectors(), layout_tracks(), layout_params() export the layout as plain data frames.
  • A node may occupy several radii: list it once per radius in the nodes table and the r column says which. The layers are radially aligned and take their own slots; links name their layer with from_r / to_r.
  • self_loops = TRUE draws from == to links as small loops folded toward the centre, instead of dropping them; loop_depth sets how deep they fold.
  • by = lays out one ring per group of a node-table column, each with its own node subset and ordering – the facet “B-plan” (spec §9.1). Finish with facet_wrap(~ <the same column>). Chords, node geoms and tracks all work per panel; track rows are placed by their own group’s node table, so the track data needs the grouping column too.
  • facet_wrap() splits chords per panel while the node ring is shared (the A-plan; by = is the alternative).

Rendering

  • Chords use circlize’s geometry: a quadratic Bezier in the plane, sampled by arc length, closed by the two node arcs. Ribbons keep their width across and meet the ring flush.
  • Ribbons carry no outline by default (colour = NA, matching circlize’s link.border = NA); type = "line" chords draw black.
  • Overlapping ribbons blend by alpha, so crossings read as a darker tint rather than a hole.
  • geom_node_arc() sits at r = 1 (offset = 0), sharing an edge with the ribbon feet. Pass offset = for a visible gap.

Inputs

  • columns = maps a link table whose endpoints are spelled differently: ggcircos(blast, columns = c(from = "qaccver", to = "saccver")). The rename copies, so the caller’s frame is untouched, and the columns you did not map travel with the link table – weight = pident and aes(fill = pident) still reach them. Covers BLAST table output, GFF3, BED and anything else without a method per format.

Tracks

  • A track with several rows per node now splits the node’s arc between them, whatever the geometry. geom = "col" used to stack every row on the whole arc, so three measurements per node drew as one solid band with no relief, and geom = "area" could not express a coverage profile at all. Only geom = "boxplot" keeps the full arc, since its stat aggregates the rows into one mark. A track with one row per node is unchanged, bin for bin.
  • geom_track_axis() no longer needs limits repeated: omitting it takes the range from the track layer filling that band, so the axis cannot label a span the values were not scaled against. Pass limits to override it.

Labels

  • geom_node_text(repel = TRUE) staggers labels that would collide: walking the ring in angle order, one that lands within a line height of its neighbour moves outward along its own radius. The angle never changes, so every label stays on its node’s spoke. ggrepel is not used here – it resolves collisions in a rectangular space and lines the labels up flat.

Layering

  • ggcircos() returns a plot that carries the link table but no mapping. x/y/xend/yend are mapped by geom_chord() itself, so a standard ggplot2 layer needs only its own aes() and data:

    ggcircos(m) + geom_rect(data = nd, aes(xmin = r, xmax = r + 0.04,
                                       ymin = theta0, ymax = theta1))

    Previously the chord columns sat on the plot, and every layer inherited them, which meant geom_rect() failed on the inherited x/y and each layer had to opt out with inherit.aes = FALSE.

Behaviour notes

  • Each sector carries a wider gap at both of its ends, so sectors read as separate blocks. The angular budget reserves one seam per sector, and sector_gap is clamped to 0.2 / S.
  • scales = "free" on a track scales each node against its own range, not against the whole column.
  • geom_node_text() rejects aes(angle = ) with ggcircos_error_data, since the coordinate owns the rotation; use rotate = TRUE.
  • A violin crossing the angular seam is cut at it and continued on the other side, so the outline is never squished into a flat edge. A density curve is split at the seam without adding vertices, so the stroke stays a stroke.
  • stack = TRUE is refused for "boxplot", "violin" and "density": their stat folds a node’s rows into one mark, so there is nothing left to stack.
  • position_track() holds only vectors (band, the node column name, the normalisation settings), so one position can be shared by several layers. A layer may take its band from it instead of repeating band =.

Not yet

An angular axis, interactive output. See vignette("from-circlize").

Deprecated shims

geom_circos(), geom_curve_link(), geom_link_lab() still run with a deprecation warning and map onto the new API; they will be removed in 0.2.0.
